evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Chinese Character Structure Database
evidence.field: 伯字形演變；白、伯字用關係
evidence.text: The entry for 伯 states that 白 was its original graph: early forms depict a thumb, which it interprets as leading to the seniority/leader sense 伯; it says 白 was commonly used for 伯 in oracle inscriptions and was later borrowed for the color word, after which 人 was added to distinguish 伯. This is the database’s account, not an uncontested conclusion.
evidence.title: 漢字「伯」：字形演變

evidence.source: Wang Ning, Fudan University Center for the Study of Excavated Texts and Ancient Chinese Characters
evidence.field: reported early uses; competing interpretations; loan direction
evidence.text: The 2010 article reports oracle-bone uses of 白 for the color word, 伯, and a place name. It surveys competing proposals for the graph’s referent and argues that 白 pictures a cooking or measuring vessel; under that author’s account, color 白 and 伯 are homophonic loans from the vessel graph. The article does not establish a dated order among those uses or provide an independently recoverable name and pronunciation for the proposed vessel.
evidence.title: 王寧：再說“白”字之本義

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: oracle-bone uses; 百; reported dated artifact/text identifiers
evidence.text: The database presents the thumb interpretation attributed to Guo Moruo, deriving 伯 from the thumb’s leading position, and describes the color use as a loan. It reports oracle-bone uses for place names, 伯, white, and 百, citing examples by corpus identifiers (including 合集36511, 30022, 9177正, and 1039); it also gives later bronze, Warring States, Qin-slip, and Han-slip examples. These reported identifiers and period labels are not equivalent to independently checked artifact dates, and the entry’s account conflicts with Wang Ning’s proposed vessel analysis and 百 analysis.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析

search_audit.query: 白 字 先用为 伯 后借为 白色 甲骨文 字源 说法
search_audit.outcome: Search surfaced the Academia Sinica account that 白 was used for 伯 before being borrowed for the color word, Wang Ning’s rival vessel account, and a CUHK database entry. Opened all three pages and inspected their contents.

search_audit.query: 白 伯 假借 甲骨文 本义 王宁 再说白字本义
search_audit.outcome: Search results repeated the competing accounts. The opened Fudan article explicitly discusses the disputed referent and the author’s proposed vessel; opened database pages supplied their respective accounts and cited examples.

gaps: The sources disagree on the graph’s original referent and on the direction of the relationship between the 伯 and color uses: Academia Sinica gives 白 → 伯 by semantic development from a thumb and later borrowing for color; Wang Ning treats both 伯 and color 白 as loans from a proposed vessel graph. The inspected sources do not settle this direction, so the directed development from color 白 to 伯 should be removed or represented as unresolved.

The reports of oracle-bone uses do not establish which sense was first: no individual inscription contexts with independently verified dates were inspected. CUHK supplies corpus identifiers, but this research did not verify those inscriptions against primary facsimiles or dating records.
No independently established ancient vessel name or pronunciation supports Wang Ning’s vessel proposal. A reconstruction of 白 itself cannot establish the name or sound of the depicted object.

The CUHK page describes 白 as borrowed for the numeral 百 and provides oracle-bone examples, while Wang Ning proposes a different vessel/content account for 百. This research does not establish a secure semantic link or earliest dated 百 use.
The competing source accounts do not alter the supplied glyph selections: this research did not inspect the glyph images or find evidence requiring a caption or selection correction.
